public_rationale: On November 29, 2023, OpenAI reported that it had lost no employees through that month's crisis [e1]. That report indicates the crisis did not trigger the forecast's departure condition, but it does not establish subsequent workforce history or offers following a qualifying departure [e1]. It therefore leaves the conditional forecast unresolved [e1].
limitations: The retention statement covers the November 2023 crisis, not the full period through October 28, 2026.
The packet does not establish a qualifying workforce departure followed by offers for the remaining assets.
The required proportion of departing staff, substantial-offer threshold and assets included remain unspecified.

statement.excerpt: (And if the OpenAI staff leaves, nobody will offer much for what’s left over.)
statement.document_title: Top 5 reasons why OpenAI was probably never really worth $86 billion

our_interpretation: The antecedent means a workforce-wide or overwhelming-majority departure that leaves the company substantially without its operating team.
Individual executive departures and ordinary employee turnover do not establish that antecedent.
Much means a substantial offer relative to the surrounding $86 billion valuation discussion; Marcus supplies no numerical cutoff.
No deadline is stated, so the forecast remains open-ended.
criteria.support_condition: After the qualifying departure, a documented and completed sale process establishes only small offers for the remaining company or assets relative to the cited valuation.
criteria.contradiction_condition: After the qualifying departure, at least one credible, substantial offer is made for the remaining company or assets.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Verify a workforce-wide or overwhelming-majority departure and identify the remaining assets. A credible substantial offer would contradict the claim; a completed disposal of all relevant assets after a documented sale process establishing only small offers would support it. Assess offers against a defensible threshold relative to the cited $86 billion valuation.
